title: Who Takes the Fast Lane? Multifamily Permit Streamlining in California
abstract: This paper studies the take-up and supply effects of California's statutory effort to streamline multifamily housing projects through Senate Bill 35. Using project-level data on 190,000 housing applications, I show that the policy's take-up among developers is strikingly low and trace the shortfall, in part, to the law's wage requirements. Formal legal reform is distinct from effective reform, and streamlined pathways can only increase supply if incentives are such that developers use these pathways.
